question: How does CPython's Reference Counter determine the exact instant an object's memory can be safely deallocated?

options.text: Whenever a variable goes out of scope or is reassigned, obrefcnt is decremented.
1. Source Code (.py) 2. Token Stream (Tokenizer / Lexer) 3. Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) (Parser) 4. Bytecode (.pyc / code objects) (Compiler)...
Because each object still holds a reference to the other, both objects maintain an obrefcnt >= 1 even when all external variables pointing to them have been deleted.

explanation: Whenever a variable goes out of scope or is reassigned, obrefcnt is decremented. The instant obrefcnt == 0, CPython immediately frees the memory back to the memory allocator.
